question.knowledge_point: Using Row Operations to Create a Column of Zeros in a 4x4 Matrix
question.problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ -7 & 2 & -6 & -7 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}],\,B=[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ -18 & -7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the matrices $A$ and $B$ above. By applying three matrix elementary row operations 

I. ${R}_{2}:=…$

II. ${R}_{3}:=…$

III. ${R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}$

each of the form ${R}_{i}:={R}_{i}+k{R}_{1},$ the matrix $A$ can be transformed into the matrix $B.$ What are the missing elementary row operations?
question.worked_solution:
To transform $A$ into $B,$ we need to make entries below ${a}_{13}=3$ equal to $0.$

To do this, we can apply the following elementary row operations:

$$
\begin{aligned}A & =[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ -7 & 2 & -6 & -7 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ -8 & 6 & -3 & 8 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ 0 & 1 & 6 & 9\end{aligned}] &  & \,\begin{aligned}{R}_{4}:={R}_{4}-2{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}9 & 4 & 3 & 4 \\ 11 & 10 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 10 & 0 & 12 \\ -18 & -7 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =B\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the missing elementary row operations are

$\,$ ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1}\,$ and $\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{1}.$
